name: send_message
description: Send a WhatsApp message to {{OWNER}}. This is the ONLY way to reach them. Text you return at the end of a turn is a fallback inside a conversation, and nothing at all from a scheduled task. Plain text, no markdown: no headings, bold, bullet lists or tables. Keep messages short and vary their length naturally. If an answer would be dense, send several short messages split at thought boundaries. Do not pad a short answer.

text.description: Message text. Plain, short, no markdown.

image_path.description: Path to an image file: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

video_path.description: Path to a video file: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

audio_path.description: Path to an audio file: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

file_path.description: Path to any other file to send as a WhatsApp document: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

name: react
description: React to a message with an emoji. Often the right answer instead of a message: acknowledging something, agreeing, or when the emoji is the whole reply. Costs them nothing to read.

message_id.description: Internal event id of the message to react to, e.g. msg_a1b2. Not a WhatsApp id.

name: schedule
description: Schedule a one-shot or recurring background task. Use this for anything time-based; never install a cron job or launchd plist. All times are this machine's local time. The run happens on a fresh thread in its own task directory with no memory of this conversation, so write `prompt` as standalone instructions: what to do, where to look, and what is worth messaging {{OWNER}} about. The response echoes back the resolved first run. Check it says what you meant.

prompt.description: Standalone instructions for the worker. It has no conversation context. Say what to do, where the inputs are, and when to message {{OWNER}} versus finish silently.

timing.description: When to run. One-shot: {"type":"once","at":"2026-08-18T07:30:00+05:30"}, RFC3339 with an offset, and it must be in the future. Recurring: {"type":"recurring","rrule":"..."} where rrule is either a cron expression evaluated in local time or a fixed interval EVERY_15M / EVERY_2H / EVERY_3D. Cron is ordinary 5-field crontab: "30 7 * * *" is 07:30 daily, "0 9 * * MON" is 09:00 Mondays, "0 18 * * MON-FRI" is weekday evenings. Day-of-week numbers follow crontab (0 and 7 are Sunday), but prefer the three-letter names, they cannot be misread. An unparseable rrule is rejected, not silently turned into something else.

at.description: One-shot only. RFC3339 with a UTC offset. Must be in the future.

rrule.description: Recurring only. Cron expression in local time, or EVERY_<n>M / EVERY_<n>H / EVERY_<n>D.

tier.description: How much model to spend on each run. 'routine' (gpt-5.6-luna, low effort) for mechanical work of known shape. Checks, sweeps, assembling a brief from known sources. This is the right answer for most schedules. 'default' (gpt-5.6-luna, xhigh) when the run needs real judgement. 'heavy' (gpt-5.6-sol, high) only when the thinking is genuinely hard, or {{OWNER}} asked for sol. Defaults to 'routine'.

name: list_schedules
description: List active schedules with their next run in local time and their tier. Use it before creating something that may already exist, and to check that a schedule you just made fires when you intended.

name: cancel_schedule
description: Cancel an active schedule. A recurring task that has stopped being useful is clutter someone will eventually have to ask about, so cancel it rather than leaving it running.

schedule_id.description: Schedule ID to cancel, e.g. sched_a1b2
